parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, entry ban or facility exclusion is documented, and 2023 polling shows majority support for equal rights, which limits everyday severity. Against that, a May 2026 warrantless raid detaining about 30 people at an LGBTQ+ venue, with alleged extortion and a baseless homosexuality charge, plus 2024 reporting of intensified persecution after a disputed election, documents police as an active risk. There is no hate-crime or gender-identity anti-discrimination recourse to remedy an outing, so extortion, detention or discriminatory service denial would go largely unpunished. Street acceptance moderates, but state-targeting and absent recourse dominate if outed.

entry_documents.protection: Not documented. Visitor uses home passport; absence of domestic gender-recognition procedure is resident-facing per rubric, not a visitor exposure.
entry_documents.interaction: Not documented for borders, scanners, or foreign-document acceptance.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: May 2026 raid: about 30 detained, warrantless entry alleged, extortion, false homosexuality charge with no legal basis.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No criminalisation of consensual same-sex conduct; no documented trans-specific custody placement rule.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police action contradicts formal legality, indicating outed visitors cannot rely on statute alone during police encounters.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented for bathrooms, wards, shelters or custody placement by sex.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Only subnational variation documented is the single raid state/province; no regional protective regime is documented.

care_services.exposure: No general healthcare or transition-care provisions documented; specific visitor care denial not documented.
care_services.interaction: Absence of resident transition-care law is a climate signal only, not rated as a visitor ban.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police accused detainees of homosexuality despite no such crime; 2015 openly gay parliamentarian held as prisoner of conscience; 2024 intensified persecution after disputed election.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct, age of consent 16 equally applied; 2016 resolution marking anti-homophobia day, later suspended.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Formal legality coexists with extortionate enforcement and political persecution, weakening paper protection.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for travelling minors, school, healthcare or family separation of visitors.
minors_guardians.protection: 2016 supreme court allowed registration with both mothers' surnames and state protection of all families without distinction; lesbian IVF access.
minors_guardians.interaction: Resident family protections do not document visitor minor safeguards; no child-specific visitor restriction documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No hate-crime statute or gender-identity anti-discrimination law, so bias violence/discrimination carries no dedicated penalty; police were alleged perpetrators in 2026 raid.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2023 poll: majority support equal rights for LGBTIQ+ people, suggesting social acceptance; government participation in Pride reported.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Supportive public attitudes may reduce street hostility, but police-as-perpetrator evidence negates expectation of police protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No working gender-recognition route, no anti-discrimination/hate-crime recourse; outcome of 2026 raid complaints not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented. Stalled 2017 constitutional action has granted no name/gender changes.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absent recourse means documented police extortion, if repeated, has no shown remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in police stops, extortion and weak court remedy, but this dossier shows no routine identity-check regime, no fines system for presentation, and no imprisonment pattern; a single large raid is less universal than 0.35-B's routine practice, so this sits above 0.35.

0.55-B involves administrative secondary screening, refused entry and slow appeals without criminalisation. This case has no documented border screening regime and stronger majority acceptance, but has documented warrantless raid/extortion and political persecution, placing it below 0.55.

0.75-C has documented respectful border practice, tribunal appeals, counsel access and compensation for unlawful detention. This dossier documents none of those operative protections and instead police extortion with no recourse, so it is materially below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: formal non-criminalisation and majority public support lower street-level severity, yet the operative interaction is police power without recourse. A visitor outed at a venue, to police, or in a political-crisis context faces the documented 2026 pattern - detention, extortion and baseless accusation - with no hate-crime or anti-discrimination remedy and no shown investigation. No universal border/facility/custody exposure or imprisonment-for-trans-status regime is documented, so risk does not reach the 0.35 universal-exclusion tier. Net: elevated risk, above 0.35, below 0.55.
